guarantees.text: It returns a function that, when called, resets a resettable atom to its initial value.
The default value comes from the read function, so `atomWithDefault((get) => get(count1Atom) * 2)` with `count1Atom` equal to 1 has the value 2.
After the value is overwritten with `set`, the read function is no longer used and a change in dependency atoms does not update the value.
Setting the atom to `RESET` discards changes made with `set` and restores the value computed by the read function.
The initial value is computed at the first use of the atom in the store, not when the atom is defined.
The initial value is recreated exactly once per store, so a new store created with `createStore()` computes a new initial value.
After initialization the atom behaves like a regular primitive atom and can be written to.
Calling `set` with zero arguments forces the read function to be reevaluated.
Calling `set` with one or more arguments calls the `write` function.
It works exactly like a primitive atom with `initialValue`, and can also be set to `RESET`.
Setting the atom to `RESET` returns it to its `initialValue`.

units.returns: (unknownStorage: AsyncStorage<unknown> | SyncStorage<unknown>) => { getItem: (key: string, initialValue: Value) => Value | PromiseLike<Value>; setItem: (key: string, newValue: unknown) => PromiseLike<void>; removeItem: (key: string) => PromiseLike<void>; subscribe?: Subscribe<unknown>; } | { getItem: (key: string, initialValue: Value) => Value | PromiseLike<Value>; setItem: (key: string, newValue: unknown) => void; removeItem: (key: string) => void; subscribe?: Subscribe<unknown>; }

guarantees.text: The storage it creates serializes with `JSON.stringify()` and deserializes with `JSON.parse()`.
It takes a getter function that returns the underlying string storage, such as `window.localStorage` or `window.sessionStorage`.
Its optional `replacer` option is used for `JSON.stringify` and its optional `reviver` option is used for `JSON.parse`.
When no `storage` is given, the atom uses `localStorage` for storage and retrieval, with `JSON.stringify()` and `JSON.parse()` for serialization and deserialization.
The `getOnInit` option is `false` by default, so on initialization the atom holds `initialValue` rather than the stored value.
With `getOnInit` set to `true` the atom returns the stored value immediately on initialization instead of `initialValue`.
The default storage subscribes to `storage` events for cross-tab synchronization.
Writing the `RESET` symbol to the atom deletes the item from storage.
With an asynchronous storage the atom value becomes async, so an updater function receives a promise or a value.

units.returns: Atom<Slice | unique symbol> & { init?: unique symbol; }

guarantees.text: The default `equalityFn` is `Object.is`, which is reference equality.
The derived atom is updated only if `equalityFn` reports that the selected value has changed.
The `selector` runs whenever the original atom changes.
It returns an atom holding a list of atoms, one for each element of the list in the original atom.
The returned atom accepts a dispatch function on write with the actions "remove", "insert" and "move", for example `{ type: "remove", atom }`.
The optional second argument `keyExtractor` is used to keep the sub-atoms stable and to prevent recreating a sub-atom when indexes shift in the source array.
While the promise is pending, the unwrapped atom has the value `undefined` when no fallback is given.
With the fallback `(prev) => prev ?? 0` the value is `0` initially, and after an update the previous resolved value is kept while pending.
Errors from the async atom are not caught and are thrown when the unwrapped atom is read.
